az_lunchbox_the.blurb: The Lunchbox is a tall freestanding formation among the towers of Lower Devil's East, off Queen Creek Canyon in central Arizona. It holds eight traditional single-pitch lines, a few reaching about 150 feet, with grades running from 5.7 up to 5.10. Most sit in the 5.8 to 5.9 band, so it suits climbers who are comfortable placing their own gear on moderate cracks. The rock is described as generally good, and excellent on some of the lines. Bring a full rack with doubles in the small cam sizes, as the surrounding area is protected almost entirely by gear.

az_sean_s_wall.blurb: Sean's Wall is a tall south-facing cliff in a ravine in the Granite Dells near Prescott, tucked just beside the Co-op area in the High Rappel zone. Eight mostly trad routes span easy to moderate: the left side is quality low-angle slab climbing, while the right side turns steeper and more varied. Grades run from about 5.5 to 5.10. Upper anchors are awkward to reach by scrambling, and the lower ones need exposed traversing, so leading is the usual choice; a 60 m rope is enough and a shorter one will not work. Parties of mixed ability can all find something here.

az_7_pumpkin_patch.blurb: Pumpkin Patch is a recently developed alcove on the Farmhouse cliff band near Sonoita in southern Arizona, set at roughly 5,200 feet. It is all sport climbing, with eight routes that reach from about 5.7 to the low 5.12s, and the bulk of them in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, so it leans toward intermediate and strong climbers. The routes are described as stretching a rope on generally good rock. The wall catches morning sun and is shaded by midday, which helps on warm days. The walk in is the same as for the neighbouring Vineyard wall and takes a half hour or more.

az_thor_s_wall.blurb: Thor's Wall sits on the west shore of Watson Lake in the Granite Dells outside Prescott. It is a steep north-facing wall, so it sees little direct sun, with bolted lines and gear routes plus some boulders on the rock above. Eight routes run from 5.10 into the 5.13 range, mostly sport with a few trad lines at 5.10, which makes it a wall for climbers already comfortable on harder grades. The rock is described as good. Finding it is part of the visit: it is hidden in a vegetated side canyon, and the big overhanging central dihedral under a roof, with bolts visible, marks the spot.
